Distortion of distances by a projected CRS

Source: R/crs.R
crs_distortion.Rd

Measures how much a projected coordinate reference system (CRS) stretches or shrinks distances over the region the data cover.

Usage

crs_distortion(data, crs = NULL)

Arguments

data

An sf or sfc object of points or polygons, in any CRS.

crs

The projected CRS to assess, as an EPSG code, a string or an sf crs object. With NULL, the default, the CRS of data, which must then be projected.

Value

A data frame with one row and the columns

max_error_pct

the distortion of distances, in percent

max_anisotropy_pct

the anisotropy, in percent

min_scale, max_scale

the smallest and largest scale factors over the region

n_locations

the number of locations at which they were computed

Details

At each location of the region, the CRS maps a small circle on the WGS 84 ellipsoid to an ellipse whose semi-axes, relative to the circle, are the largest and smallest scale factors there (Tissot's indicatrix). They are computed from the derivatives of the projection by central differences over 10 m. The distortion is the largest of the differences between these scale factors and 1 over the region. It also bounds the relative error of the distance between any two locations of the region, because the straight line between them in the plane and the shortest path between them on the Earth both stay within the region, or very close to it for a region thousands of kilometres across.

The region is the convex hull of the data, whether points or polygons, so that it holds the paths between them, for example across the sea between islands. It is represented by up to 2,000 vertices of the data, its boundary and a grid of points inside it.

The anisotropy is the largest ratio of the two scale factors at a location, minus 1. It is zero, up to rounding, for a conformal CRS, such as UTM or any CRS from propose_crs(), so that distances from a location are changed by the same factor in every direction. An equal-area CRS changes them more in some directions than in others.

See also

propose_crs()

Examples

data("infect_sma")
# The UTM zone proposed for the data
crs_distortion(infect_sma, crs = propose_crs(infect_sma, messages = FALSE))
#>   max_error_pct max_anisotropy_pct min_scale max_scale n_locations
#> 1    0.01482633       1.490337e-06 0.9998517 0.9999534        1970
# Pseudo-Mercator, which is not conformal
crs_distortion(infect_sma, crs = 3857)
#>   max_error_pct max_anisotropy_pct min_scale max_scale n_locations
#> 1      28.80057          0.4108479  1.279101  1.288006        1970
